title: Small CLI with a stated exit code contract
prompt:
Build a single Python file named `wcl.py`, a command line tool run as `python3 wcl.py [--min-words N] FILE...`.

For each FILE, in the order given, print one line to stdout: `<lines> <words> <bytes> <name>` (counts separated by single spaces, `<name>` exactly as given; `lines` is the number of newline characters, `words` is the number of whitespace separated tokens, `bytes` is the file size in bytes).

Exit code contract:
- 0: every file was read and (if `--min-words` is given) every file has at least N words.
- 1: at least one FILE could not be read. Print `wcl: <name>: cannot read` to stderr for each such file and still process the remaining files. This takes precedence over 3.
- 2: usage error (no FILE given, `--min-words` without a non-negative integer, or an unknown option). Print a message to stderr and nothing to stdout.
- 3: all files were read but at least one has fewer than N words.

Use only the standard library. Keep everything in `wcl.py`.
